DeepWalk, in its original form, does not use hyperbolic Poincaré ball optimization, Riemannian gradient descent, or Möbius gyrovector addition; those are components of hyperbolic embedding methods, not the standard DeepWalk algorithm. DeepWalk instead learns node embeddings from truncated random walks and a Skip-gram objective in Euclidean space.

If you are asking for the Poincaré distance formula used in hyperbolic embeddings, the distance between two points u and v inside the Poincaré ball model is

d(u, v) = arcosh\left(1 + 2\,\frac{\|u-v\|^2}{(1-\|u\|^2)(1-\|v\|^2)}\right),

where \|u\| and \|v\| are Euclidean norms and both points must lie strictly inside the unit ball (\|u\| < 1, \|v\| < 1). This metric grows rapidly near the boundary of the ball, which is why the model is well suited to representing tree-like hierarchies with low distortion.

So, under your assumption, the relevant distance is the Poincaré metric above; but for actual DeepWalk, there is no Poincaré distance formula because the method is not a hyperbolic model.
